thread:
Nina: Quick follow-up on API-key scoping RFC. We still lack a safe fallback when project-scoped write keys expire mid-ingest. Ideas?
Omar: We hit this in staging: writers kept using cached project keys and failed. No clear fallback path.
Priya: What about an exchange flow that returns a narrow org:read token when project:write is rejected? With strict gating.
Nina: Gate how?
Priya: Require mTLS svc cert + service allowlist flag (allow_exchange=true) + authz check. Emit audit_id each exchange.
Quinn: Ops concern: thundering exchanges. Add client jitter/backoff + server per-service rate limit and Retry-After.
Omar: Client guidance: base=150ms, factor=2, max_attempts=4, jitter=0-100ms. Upstream should cache exchanged token to avoid fanout storms.
Nina: Runbook sketch: alert on auth.expired.rate spike -> identify service -> if allow_exchange -> automated one-shot exchange -> if fail: pause writes + page SRE.
Priya: Exchange API example: POST /auth/exchange Authorization: Bearer <token> {"target":"org:read"} -> returns token, expires_in=600, audit_id.
security-bot: Note: policy reminder: allow_exchange default OFF. Requests require platform+security approval.
Quinn: Telemetry: add labels service, project, exchange_attempted, exchange_result. Track auth.exchange.rate by service.
Nina: Agreed. Next: Priya to open API PR, Quinn to add runbook steps, Omar to update SDK retry doc.
Priya: Will include server-side rate limiting and audit events in PR.
Nina: Thanks — tagging @oncall when runbook is live.
